source.title: Asymptotic Behavior of Multi--Task Learning: Implicit Regularization and Double Descent Effects
source.authors: Ayed M. Alrashdi; Oussama Dhifallah; Houssem Sifaou

record.tranche_reason: Tests double-descent behavior in a new setting: multi-task linear regression and binary classification, including how task combination and regularization affect the curves.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own asymptotic analysis and simulation results for generalization error as κ=k/n varies, and for regularization-strength sweeps. Theoretical curves and simulation comparisons are not results from other work. The number-of-tasks sweeps measure a different axis from the listed claim versions and are recorded under fits_no_version. The paper does not test epoch-wise behavior or vary sample size independently.
record.test_reason: The paper's own asymptotic theory and simulations trace generalization error against κ=k/n. Here k is the number of fitted parameters and p/n is fixed, so this is a model-size sweep in linear regression and linear classifiers. It shows a double-descent peak at the interpolation threshold and reports how multi-task regularization (γ2) and the number of combined tasks move, shrink or remove the peak. This bears on V4 (non-deep model classes) and on the regularization part of V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The multi-task formulation is asymptotically equivalent to a traditional formulation with added regularization that favours solutions aligned with the generative model. Empirically, combining tasks postpones double descent and can mitigate it asymptotically.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes a multi-task convex formulation for misspecified perceptron-style linear regression and binary classification using asymptotic CGMT analysis and simulations; it does not reproduce a deep-network size sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The interpolation threshold and double-descent strength vary with the number of combined tasks and with regularization strength γ2; the text also reports dependence on task similarity ρ.

fits_no_version.finding: Generalization error decreases as the number of combined tasks grows (Fig 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In regularized multi-task linear models, combining more related tasks lowers generalization error.

fits_no_version.finding: The interpolation-threshold location in κ shifts from κ⋆ toward Tκ⋆ as the number of tasks or γ2 increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In multi-task linear models, the peak location scales with the effective pooled sample size set by task coupling.

record.problems: The empirical evidence is based on numerical simulations under stated Gaussian and high-dimensional assumptions, not deep networks or a broad set of model classes. Several plotted values are not given numerically in the text. The study does not test epochs, independently varied sample size, label-noise dependence, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 7's generalization-error change with task similarity ρ is not a result about the listed size, epoch, sample-size, or complexity-axis versions. No other reported results on the listed axes were omitted.

untested.parts: No deep networks; only linear regression and linear classifiers.
Training time or epochs are not varied.
Sample size is not varied on its own at fixed model size.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across axes.
Label noise or variance as the driver of the peak is not varied. Multiple or triple peaks are not studied. Optimal tuning of the ridge parameter γ1 is not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The κ=k/n sweep at fixed α=p/n is a parameter-count sweep in misspecified linear models, so V4 applies and V1 does not. The record's 'challenges' label on V4 for Fig 6 is replaced with limits_scope: the missing peak there comes from regularization, which bears on V6 rather than contradicting V4. All evidence is figure-only, with no numeric values in the text; the results are Gaussian-design asymptotics checked by Monte Carlo simulation.

versions.untested_parts: The tested models are linear regression and binary classification models, not deep networks.
Training epochs or training time are not varied.
The number of training samples is not independently varied near the interpolation threshold.
The experiments concern the paper's multi-task linear regression and binary classification formulations, not a broad survey of model classes.
The paper does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across axes.

Regularization strength is varied and its effect on double descent is reported. Label-noise or variance as the peak's driver, multiple peaks, and disappearance under optimally tuned regularization are not tested.
The paper does not re-count complexity using an effective number of parameters or test whether that yields an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.measure: Generalization error as κ varies; double-descent mitigation.

rows.note: The text says combining a large number of tasks mitigates double descent and leads to generalization error that is strictly decreasing in κ.
rows.check: The peak is absent here because combining many tasks is equivalent to added ridge plus alignment regularization. Calling this a challenge to V4 overstates it. It is a regularized setting, and it bears on V6, where regularization removing the peak counts as observed.
